doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Is his music experimental?
summary: Zeitlin says he tries to push his own envelope and stay organic rather than calling the music experimental.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I’ve been listening to your music for a long time and it always seems fairly experimental. Would you think of it in that manner?

I don’t know about experimental. I do like to feel that I’m pushing my own envelope when I play, that I am reaching and trying to stretch the boundaries of what material I’m working with to try to come up with something fresh and to have it be organic.
Organic. Okay. I know you work with the standards but you’re also a composer yourself.
